gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-mro: Visitor looks like a pixel-era readout, with gaping e shapes and short ascenders above big bowls. Noto Sans Mro is the opposite, dense and tall through the middle, so paragraphs would feel compact and modern.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-multani: Tall and lofty in the lowercase, Noto Sans Multani keeps its e wide at the terminal and reads with an easy, modern lift. Visitor is best at a loud, uniform, nostalgic shout, while the body font handles the sustained talking.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Noto Sans Myanmar lays down a thick, heavy-looking strip of text with a broad c that feels welcoming and clean. Under Visitor's flat, unvarying strokes, a long page would read steadily.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-nag-mund: Zero stroke modulation is Visitor's whole personality: every line the same, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders over big bowls. Noto Sans Nag Mundari does the quieter work, its half-unwrapped c and s and capital-sized lowercase carrying text in a contemporary sans voice.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-nandinag: Bent copper pipe, basically: Visitor's tubular strokes and gaping e give the heading a retro digital bite, while its short ascenders sit over big bowls. Noto Sans Nandinagari follows with generous openings and a big lowercase, friendly beside it.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-newa: Visitor cuts its letters like bent wire, with gaping e mouths and short ascenders above big bowls, all nostalgic and digital. Noto Sans Newa brings a clearly open e and tall bowls, a modern counterweight.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Nostalgic glass-tube letters carry the heading in Visitor, gaping e and all, with short ascenders over big bowls. Noto Sans Nushu answers with a towering x-height and terminals held far from the stroke, a plain sans that feels modern.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Clean and contemporary, Noto Sans Ogham opens its e wide, and its tall bodies make the lowercase look bold. Visitor does its best work as a uniform-gauge, nostalgic headline, while the body font is built for the running text.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Clean and contemporary, Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so words read as solid blocks, not skylines. Beside Visitor's marker-tip letters, a long page would feel tidy.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-old-hung: Approachable and contemporary, Noto Sans Old Hungarian keeps large open counters in its tall a, e and s, even at tiny sizes. Visitor is best as flat, contrast-free nostalgia in big letters, while the body font is best at staying legible.
